content: Speaking at the first convocation of Amal College of Advanced Studies (Autonomous) at Nilambur, Higher Education Minister Roji M. content: It comprises 14 members of BJP and five of Congress. It also has two members each from JD(U), TMC and DMK, and one member each from SP, IUML, Shiv Sena, NCP (SP), NCP and TDP.

title: BCCI’s big plan for Sooryavanshi: ‘Serve like Sachin, not be a one-year wonder’
content: The BCCI is diligently tracking 15-year-old Vaibhav Sooryavanshi's development in cricket. With his remarkable debut as India's youngest men's international player following an explosive IPL performance, the board aims to capitalise on his promise for a sustainable international career. They are keen to ensure he avoids being labeled a fleeting talent while closely mentoring a broader pool of young players at the Centre of Excellence.

title: Paswan vs Manjhi: SC 'creamy layer' debate divides NDA; will it open Pandora's box?
content: Two influential Dalit leaders in Bihar are embroiled in a public discourse about sub-quotas related to existing reservations. This rift within the Scheduled Caste community may stir up political complexities for the NDA government. The BJP must navigate the demands of anti-reservation activists and also its allies, who seek changes in reservation policy, even as it strives to maintain the balance of its electoral coalition pressures.

title: Bezos got a special invite to ‘US exclusive Country Club’ but won’t get membership
content: Jeff Bezos and Lauren Sanchez attended an exclusive club event as guests.  Six months later, Bezos still awaits membership despite owning island properties.  Membership at Indian Creek Country Club requires more than significant financial investment.  Other prominent residents also face challenges in securing club membership.  The club's stringent approval process emphasizes member relationships and committee decisions.

title: 8th pay commission: How level 8 staff could earn up to Rs 28.89 lakh extra in 10 yrs
content: Employee bodies have argued that the current 3% annual increment is not sufficient to keep pace with rising expenses. Their recommendations have ranged from 5% to 7%. If such proposals are accepted, a higher increment rate of 5% or 7% would have a direct impact on the salary progression of central government employees.

title: Smriti Mandhana creates history, surpasses Lanning to become leading century-maker
content: In an exhilarating display of skill, Smriti Mandhana shattered records by scoring her 18th international century, amassing 124 runs in just 64 balls. Her explosive knock led India to a formidable total of 193 runs. Shafali Verma played a vital role at the start with her brisk 28, setting the tone for a dominant batting showcase by the Indian team.

title: Meta AI chief said he wants to wait for Elon Musk’s Neuralink before having kids
content: Meta AI chief Alexandr Wang plans to delay having children until brain-computer interfaces advance. He believes children's brains can adapt better to technologies like Neuralink. Early childhood offers significant neuroplasticity for integrating new interfaces. This integration could allow children to use the technology in unique ways. Wang expects artificial intelligence to become increasingly powerful and capable.

title: Nepal floods: No bodies to cremate, kin burn kusha effigies as hopes fade for missing
content: Families in Nuwakot and Rasuwa performed symbolic cremations for missing flood victims.  Relatives used kusha grass effigies when bodies could not be recovered.  Searches for missing kin proved unsuccessful across various locations.  Priests guided families through traditional rituals for liberating souls.  Over one hundred effigies were cremated in Kathmandu's Pashupati Aryaghat.

title: Feminist icon Gloria Steinem dies at 92; tributes pour in
content: Gloria Steinem, the pioneering feminist activist, author and journalist, has passed away at 92. Following her death, Hillary Clinton, Meghan Markle, Lena Dunham and others paid heartfelt tributes, remembering her influence, generosity and lifelong fight for equality. From women’s rights to reproductive freedom, Steinem’s work inspired generations and left an enduring mark on society.

title: Jim Bishop bought Colorado land for $450 at 15, then spent 50 years on a castle
content: For over five decades, Jim Bishop dedicated his life to building the biggest one-man castle in the world, starting in 1969. His ambition was fueled by a determination to silence skeptics, initially using his own funds and later gathering donations. After Jim's passing in November 2024, his son Daniel has taken up the monumental task, ensuring the legacy of this extraordinary masterpiece lives on.

title: Apple and Google rename Lake Ontario to Lake America; one app refuses Trump’s order
content: MapQuest's refusal to comply with a federal directive to rename Lake Ontario has landed the app at the peak of the US App Store charts. Unlike Google Maps and Apple Maps, which followed the presidential order, MapQuest experienced a remarkable boost, collecting over 1.5 million downloads in North America. The company is now shifting focus towards new features that users are eager for.

title: After mother's death, Wyoming rancher vowed to protect 2,506 acres forever
content: David Ellsbury honored his late mother's wish by safeguarding the family's cherished Diamond E Ranch from development. Spanning 2,506 acres, this land is now forever shielded by a land trust, ensuring that future generations can enjoy its unspoiled beauty. The ranching traditions of the family will thrive on this preserved estate.

title: BCCI meeting decoded: Saikia reveals plans for injuries, SENA tours & 2027 WC
content: The BCCI is set to enhance its overseas performance strategy while tackling player injuries. They aim to craft a robust plan in preparation for the 2027 ODI World Cup, which will require adjustments in the Future Tours Programme to prioritise player rest. Recent defeats in white-ball matches against England and Ireland were carefully analysed, and insight was gathered from captains and the head coach regarding fitness protocols.

title: Travis Kelce’s $1.5M charity under scrutiny: Why did less go to charity?
content: Travis Kelce’s Eighty-Seven and Running Foundation is facing scrutiny over its reported spending between 2021 and 2024. The nonprofit raised $1.5 million and spent about $1.1 million, with $469,000 listed for management and $446,000 for charity. Kelce’s business manager Aaron Eanes disputed the figures, saying some charitable operational costs were misclassified. He said management fees dropped to zero in 2025 as the foundation works to improve transparency and governance.

title: Patrick and Brittany Mahomes feed 125 Kansas City families: How are they giving back?
content: Dedicated to enhancing the lives of Kansas City families, the Patrick and Brittany Mahomes’ foundation offers vital food resources through impactful partnerships. Last Thanksgiving, their efforts resulted in over 200 families receiving festive meal packages. Moreover, the foundation has prioritized food allergy education with a unique back-to-school event, reinforcing their commitment to community health and ensuring everyone has access to nutritious food.

title: Vanessa Trump, Tiger Woods lean on each other as their love grows, insider says
content: Vanessa Trump and Tiger Woods are standing strong for each other during difficult times. Vanessa has been battling breast cancer, while Tiger faced legal trouble after his DUI arrest. The couple has reportedly grown even closer while dealing with separate challenges. They have leaned on each other, providing significant strength during these periods. Their relationship has deepened as they navigate these trying moments together.

title: Why personal-guarantor recoveries are so tiny — and why Chandra’s was tinier still
content: Subhash Chandra was offering just 0.03% of the loans for which he was a personal guarantor. But there should be no surprise here. In the history of such settlements in India, guarantors have paid an average 1% of the amount they stood guarantee for

title: KPSC irregularities: K'taka govt suspends IAS officer facing probe
content: Karnataka government suspended IAS officer Gyanendra Kumar Gangwar due to KPSC recruitment irregularities.  He is currently in CID custody as the agency investigates the commission's alleged wrongdoings.  The Directorate of Enforcement is also conducting a separate investigation into the matter.  Gangwar served as Controller of Examinations at KPSC during the period under scrutiny.  His suspension is effective immediately pending further investigation by the CID.

title: Goa's new housing law opens the door to revenue-sharing projects; here's why
content: The Goa Assembly has passed a bill allowing the Goa Housing Board to implement projects. This new legislation enables joint ventures and revenue-sharing models for housing development. The amendment empowers the board to partner with eligible entities for scheme implementation. This move aims to leverage practical and financial advantages for efficient project execution. The state government will soon frame rules for these new development partnerships.

title: BCCI breaks silence on Asian Games concerns, promises ‘best facilities’ for Team India
content: The BCCI has responded to worries surrounding the accommodation for Indian cricket teams during the Asian Games, with secretary Devajit Saikia assuring that there are no pressing concerns. The board is dedicated to delivering high-quality amenities for both players and staff. Under VVS Laxman’s leadership, the men's team will compete, while Amol Muzumdar coaches the women's team, as India seek to retain their titles.

title: Why Agarkar was not present in BCCI's meeting? Devajit Saikia reveals the reason
content: BCCI secretary Devajit Saikia clarified the situation surrounding Ajit Agarkar's absence from a recent board meeting. He shared that Agarkar was traveling and encountered connectivity problems that prevented him from joining virtually. Saikia also brushed aside any rumors about adjustments to the senior men's selection committee. The meeting primarily reviewed past performances and strategized for the upcoming 2027 ODI World Cup without addressing the potential appointment of a cricket director.

title: Jennifer Aniston's boyfriend Jim opens up on partial paralysis due to nerve damage
content: Jim Curtis shared his journey of overcoming spinal cord lesions and partial paralysis. He spoke about accepting struggles and finding personal power through self-love. Curtis also advised on navigating life crossroads without abandoning responsibilities. Jennifer Aniston attended the event celebrating his new book, 'The Book of Possibility'. The couple has become more open about their relationship since 2025.

title: Bank holiday on Janmashtami: Where are banks closed on Sept 4, 2026? Check list
content: Indian banks across various states will be closed on September 4 to observe Krishna Janmashtami. Customers should be aware that further closures will occur throughout the month for additional festivals and elections. It's essential to check local holiday schedules for branch services, although digital banking and ATMs will continue to function normally. Plan accordingly for any urgent in-person banking needs during these times.

title: Couple buys Rs 60L flat, husband taxed on Rs 34.81L stamp-duty gap; ITAT objects
content: Can the entire difference between a property’s actual purchase price and its stamp-duty value be added to the income of just one of its co-owners? A recent ruling by ITAT Mumbai has addressed this question in a case involving a husband and wife who jointly purchased a property.

title: Punjabi singer Baljeet Singh found dead; police launch probe
content: Baljeet Singh, a popular Punjabi singer, was tragically found deceased at his home in Ludhiana, prompting a police investigation initiated by a disturbing odor. Upon arrival, officers discovered his lifeless body on the bed, accompanied by noticeable signs of blood. Disturbingly, Singh had been out of touch with his family for several days. This shocking discovery occurs shortly after the murder of another regional music artist, Ankit Balyan.

title: ‘What more do you want?’: BCCI secy’s blunt message on Rohit Sharma speculation
content: BCCI secretary Devajit Saikia defended Rohit Sharma's continued high-level performance in ODIs. He questioned the ongoing speculation regarding the veteran player's future in the team. Sharma himself has previously stated that external noise does not significantly impact his focus. The board's stance comes as the 2027 ODI World Cup approaches. India will eventually need to consider succession planning for the team.

title: Meet Pankaj Kamboj, who turned repeated defence exam setbacks into CAPF success
content: UPSC success story: Pankaj Kamboj’s journey to clearing the UPSC CAPF Assistant Commandant examination is marked by repeated setbacks across competitive exams. After failing UPSC CSE Prelims three times and facing several SSB rejections, he continued preparing through self-study while clearing CDS and AFCAT multiple times. Coming from a farming family near the Uttar Pradesh-Uttarakhand border, Kamboj credits his mother for motivating him. He has now cleared CAPF while continuing his UPSC Civil Services journey after clearing Prelims on his fourth attempt.

title: 5 migrants dead after boat carrying over 100 people drifts for weeks in Atlantic
content: At least five African migrants died after their boat encountered trouble at sea. Forty-four survivors were rescued and brought to safety near Gran Canaria. Survivors reported being adrift for nearly a month without provisions. Many migrants suffered dehydration and illness after drinking seawater. The Atlantic route to the Canary Islands remains a dangerous journey.

title: Yamunanagar woman stabbed multiple times by neighbour in front of 4-year-old son, dies
content: A 26-year-old woman died after a neighbour allegedly attacked her with a knife. The accused reportedly followed her into a house and inflicted multiple stab wounds. Police registered a murder case against the neighbour, identified as Sajan. The victim's husband stated the accused had prior disputes with the family. Authorities are actively searching for the absconding accused.

title: Bihar man lured to Delhi over old rivalry, shot dead; 8 held after 12,000-km chase
content: A Bihar resident was lured to Delhi and shot dead over an old rivalry. Eight individuals were arrested across multiple states following a large interstate operation. The victim was allegedly killed in a rented premises in southeast Delhi's Pul Prahladpur. Police investigations revealed a conspiracy involving several associates of the main accused. Efforts continue to recover remaining firearms and identify other potential accomplices.

title: ‘India lost to Ireland. Has cricket ended?’: Naqvi defends Pakistan's shake-up
content: Mohsin Naqvi, chairman of the Pakistan Cricket Board, stood firm regarding the team's latest performances and selection adjustments. He questioned whether a handful of defeats should spell the end of cricket in Pakistan. Noting other teams' challenges, he highlighted Pakistan's advancements in white-ball rankings while also tackling critiques from former players about the management's approach to team building.

title: 7.8% growth, but a Rs 6 lakh crore question: Why GDP data has sparked a debate
content: One of the biggest points of discussion and questioning is the revision to Q1 FY26 GDP at current prices, that is the figures for last year's same quarter numbers. Under the old 2011-12 series, GDP was estimated at Rs 86.05 lakh crore. However, under the new series, it has subsequently been revised to Rs 80 lakh crore.

title: Watch: Chahal’s magical delivery leaves Ben Stokes stunned in County game
content: Yuzvendra Chahal dismissed Ben Stokes with a remarkable delivery in the County Championship.  The Indian spinner's magic ball left the England all-rounder completely baffled.  Chahal claimed four wickets for 36 runs in a superb spell.  Stokes has faced difficulties against Indian spinners recently.  This dismissal highlighted Chahal's impressive performance for Northamptonshire.

title: Wai Wai under FSSAI scanner: Firm told to stop production, 32,000kg stock seized
content: Food regulator FSSAI has ordered CG Foods India to stop producing Veg Bhujia Namkeen.  Inspections revealed hygiene lapses and unlicensed manufacturing of bhujia products.  The company was found re-processing floor-collected noodles without proper heat treatment.  FSSAI seized over 32,000 kg of stock and detained expired finished goods.  Legal proceedings have been initiated against CG Foods India for these violations.

title: 'Govt aid would stop': Bengal CM warns schools over Vande Mataram compliance
content: West Bengal's Chief Minister warned schools about financial aid cuts for not singing Vande Mataram. He criticized past governments for allegedly destroying the education system and distorting curricula. The Chief Minister stated reforms are underway to restore Indian culture and nationalist values in schools. He also accused the previous government of banning the National Cadet Corps in educational institutions.

title: ‘Akash Anand needs to become more mature’: Mayawati rules out major BSP role for nephew
content: In her recent remarks, Mayawati emphasized that Akash Anand needs greater political maturity to assume significant roles within the party. She reaffirmed that the Bahujan Samaj Party intends to independently contest all upcoming elections nationwide. Additionally, she labeled the Congress party as distinctly anti-Dalit and anti-Ambedkar, and critiqued the RSS for inconsistencies between their rhetoric and actions.

title: 'How am I responsible for my daughter's comments?' Sacked T'gana minister takes on CM
content: Former minister Konda Surekha expressed her displeasure regarding her cabinet removal. She stated she committed no corruption and had responded to show-cause notices. Surekha questioned the lack of consultation and the fairness of the decision. She defended her daughter and questioned actions against other Congress leaders. The former minister has not yet decided on her future political path.
